title: Interactions between Group Theory, Symmetry and Cryptology
creator: GonzaÌlez Vasco, MariÌa Isabel$$QGonzaÌlez Vasco, MariÌa Isabel
desc: Cryptography lies at the heart of most technologies deployed today for secure communications. At the same time, mathematics lies at the heart of cryptography, as cryptographic constructions are based on algebraic scenarios ruled by group or number theoretical laws. Understanding the involved algebraic structures is, thus, essential to design robust cryptographic schemes. This Special Issue is concerned with the interplay between group theory, symmetry and cryptography. The book highlights four exciting areas of research in which these fields intertwine: post-quantum cryptography, coding theory, computational group theory and symmetric cryptography. The articles presented demonstrate the relevance of rigorously analyzing the computational hardness of the mathematical problems used as a base for cryptographic constructions. For instance, decoding problems related to algebraic codes and rewriting problems in non-abelian groups are explored with cryptographic applications in mind. New results on the algebraic properties or symmetric cryptographic tools are also presented, moving ahead in the understanding of their security properties. In addition, post-quantum constructions for digital signatures and key exchange are explored in this Special Issue, exemplifying how (and how not) group theory may be used for developing robust cryptographic tools to withstand quantum attacks.

desc: In the center of this study stood some 154 letters exchanged between the Austrian writer Alexander Lernet-Holenia (1897-1976) and Maria Charlotte ("Lotte") Sweceny (nee Stein, 1904-1956), the co-proprietor of the Viennese publishing house Manz, between 1938 and 1945. The transcripts are followed by a commentary that aims to elucidate the historical, individual and geographical references. A methodological note explains the corpus' provenance and method of transcribing and commenting on the letters adopted in the thesis. The last chapter of this study is devoted to Lotte Sweceny, the letters' addressee, and her family background. The letters' existence is due to the fact that the couple was separated by the outbreak of WW II and continued their relationship through correspondence. In September 1939 Lernet took part in the "Wehrmacht's" raid on Poland and was lightly wounded. As a result he spent the rest of the war on a leave of absence in his house in St. Wolfgang and, after September 1941, in Berlin. There, he worked as head of development of the "Heeresfilmstelle" (an office in charge of producing NS propaganda films), writing scripts himself and evaluating those by others. In these years, two of his most important novels, Mars im Widder (Mars in Aries) and both Sicily (The Two Sicilies), were written - both are today considered as running counter to NS propaganda. desc: "Both the US and the UK seemed caught off-guard by the uprisings in Libya and Egypt and policymakers had to deal with leaders that switched from being allies to 'pariahs.' This collection of essays, written by leading scholars, examines the evolution of British and American perceptions of  'adversaries' in the Middle East since the Cold War. It traces the evolution of how leaders have been perceived, what determined such perceptions, and how they can change over time. It shows that in many cases the beliefs held by policymakers have influenced their policies and the way they adapted during crisis. creator: Machado, J. A. Tenreiro, author.$$QMachado, J. A. Tenreiro
desc: In order to measure and quantify the complex behavior of real-world systems, either novel mathematical approaches or modifications of classical ones are required to precisely predict, monitor, and control complicated chaotic and stochastic processes. Though the term of entropy comes from Greek and emphasizes its analogy to energy, today, it has wandered to different branches of pure and applied sciences and is understood in a rather rough way, with emphasis placed on the transition from regular to chaotic states, stochastic and deterministic disorder, and uniform and non-uniform distribution or decay of diversity. This collection of papers addresses the notion of entropy in a very broad sense. The presented manuscripts follow from different branches of mathematical/physical sciences, natural/social sciences, and engineering-oriented sciences with emphasis placed on the complexity of dynamical systems. Topics like timing chaos and spatiotemporal chaos, bifurcation, synchronization and anti-synchronization, stability, lumped mass and continuous mechanical systems modeling, novel nonlinear phenomena, and resonances are discussed.

desc: "In 1916, a young Quaker schoolteacher and poetry scholar named Elizebeth Smith was hired by an eccentric tycoon to find the secret messages he believed were embedded in Shakespeare's plays. She moved to the tycoon's lavish estate outside of Chicago expecting to spend her days poring through old books. But the rich man's close ties to the U.S. government, and the urgencies of war, quickly transformed Elizebeth's mission. She soon learned to apply her skills to an exciting new venture: codebreaking -- the solving of secret messages without knowledge of the key. Working alongside her on the estate was William Friedman, a Jewish scientist who would become her husband and lifelong codebreaking partner. Elizebeth and William were in many ways the Adam and Eve of the National Security Agency, the U.S. institution that monitors and intercepts foreign communications to glean intelligence. creator: Daybell, James, 1972- editor.$$QDaybell, James | Gordon, Andrew, 1969- editor.$$QGordon, Andrew
desc: The letter is a powerfully evocative form that has gained in resonance as the habits of personal letter writing have declined in a digital age. But faith in the letter as evidence of the intimate thoughts of individuals underplays the sophisticated ways letters functioned in the past. In Cultures of Correspondence in Early Modern Britain leading scholars approach the letter from a variety of disciplinary perspectives to uncover the habits, forms, and secrets of letter writing. Where material features of the letter have often been ignored by past generations fixated on the text alone, contributors to this volume examine how such elements as handwriting, seals, ink, and the arrangement of words on the manuscript page were significant carriers of meaning alongside epistolary rhetorics. The chapters here also explore the travels of the letter, uncovering the many means through which correspondence reached a reader and the ways in which the delivery of letters preoccupied contemporaries. At the same time, they reveal how other practices, such as the use of cipher and the designs of forgery, threatened to subvert the surveillance and reading of letters. The anxiety of early modern letter writers over the vulnerability of correspondence is testament to the deep dependence of the culture on the letter. title: Nineteenth-century American literature and the long Civil War  / Cody Marrs, University of Georgia.
creator: Marrs, Cody, author.$$QMarrs, Cody
desc: "American literature in the nineteenth century is often divided into two asymmetrical halves, neatly separated by the Civil War. In Nineteenth-Century American Literature and the Long Civil War, Cody Marrs argues that the war is a far more elastic boundary for literary history than has frequently been assumed. Focusing on the later writings of Walt Whitman, Frederick Douglass, Herman Melville, and Emily Dickinson, this book shows how the war took imaginative shape across, and even beyond, the nineteenth century, inflecting literary forms and expressions for decades after 1865. These writers, Marrs demonstrates, are best understood not as antebellum or postbellum figures but as transbellum authors who cipher their later experiences through their wartime impressions and prewar ideals. This book is a bold, revisionary contribution to debates about temporality, periodization, and the shape of American literary history."--Back cover.

title: A splendor of letters : the permanence of books in an impermanent world  / Nicholas A. Basbanes.
creator: Basbanes, Nicholas A., 1943- author.$$QBasbanes, Nicholas A.
desc: "Basbanes now offers a consideration of the many pressing issues that surround the role of books in contemporary society, such as the willful destruction of books and libraries in Sarajevo, Tibet, and Cambodia, and the spirited efforts to restore them. The matter of "discards" at various libraries takes on an entirely new dimension as well, with fully researched stories about the kind of attitudes that may lead to the loss of last copies of important works. In vivid detail, Basbanes examines the many materials that have been used over the centuries to record information -- among them clay tablets, papyrus scrolls, slabs of stone, palm leaves, animal skins, and hammered sheets of gold and copper. Also discussed are the various debates that continue to rage about preservation, which may mean saving and storing books on paper indefinitely, or as electronic data, which are by nature ephemeral. In this beautifully packaged edition, Nicholas Basbanes brings to a close his wonderful trilogy on the remarkable world of books and bibliophiles."--Jacket

title: [Notarial cartulary for the Confraternity of the Cross in Ferrara, Italy], 1530-1586.
creator: Newberry Library. Manuscript. Case MS 5321.$$QNewberry Library.
desc: Notarial cartulary, transcribed for--and probably at--the Confraternity of the Cross in Ferrara, Italy, containing 15 documents, dated between 1530 and 1586. The documents in the register deal with donations and indulgences of the Confraternity over a period of approximately eighty years, each one witnessed by a notary, whose cipher and initials appear in the margins, next to the traditional notarial oath which begins "Ego..." Included are indulgences; copy, dated Jan. 15, 1530, of a bull by Pope Clement VII concerning the Confraternity's charter; a copy of the will of one of the Confraternity members, Father Constantino Cardano, an inventory of his property, and a memo on the execution of his will; a memo on the bequest of Domenico Bondio to the Confraternity; absolutions granted to various persons by the Confraternity; and a memo about the Confraternity's relic--a piece of wood from the Cross--and the order to make a copy in silver.

title: Agreement for tenancy of a farm in the Vale of Evesham, England, between 1860 and 1900? : incomplete manuscript.
creator: Roger S. Baskes Collection (Newberry Library)$$QRoger S. Baskes Collection (Newberry Library)
desc: Manuscript lease regarding a farm in Worcester County, England. Lease discusses that the yearly rent of the farm is 1,250 pounds or 20 pounds per acre. The tenant is responsible for maintaining the entire farm including all fruit trees using the best methods known to Worchester and the Vale of Evesham code. During the last 5 years of tenancy, the tenant should not plant any exhausting crops or there will be a penalty of 5 of 10 pounds an acre. Potatoes are the only crop that may leave the farm if other root crops, corn, hay, manure, compost, straw, etc. leave the farm there will be a fine of 5 pounds. The tenant is not allowed to sell hay or straw produced on the farm. The outgoing tenant will be compensated if all manure from the last harvest, root crops, seeds, and artificial grass has been left on the property and maintained properly for the incoming tenant.

title: Agenda de bufete o libro de memoria diario para 1884 con noticias y guia de Madrid.
creator: Rizal, José, 1861-1896.$$QRizal, José
desc: Printed diary for 1884, with handwritten entries for 1 Jan.-1 Nov. made by José Rizal as a twenty-three year-old student of art and medicine in Madrid. The entries contain Rizal's descriptions of his meetings in the cafés of Madrid with friends such as the Paterno brothers, Esteban Villanueva, Graciano López Jaena, Eduardo de Lete, and Valentín Ventura; his medical classes at the University and drawing classes at the Academia de San Fernando, as well as student strikes and protests; outings to the theatre; and references to political topics.  There are frequent references to the "Círculo", a society of Filipino residents of Madrid, founded in 1882, whose publication, "Revista del Círculo Hispano-Filipino" was strongly anti-Spanish. In addition, Rizal mentions books by Horace, Dumas, Voltaire, and Eugenio Sue--El judío errante--and records his daily expenditures for items such as food, paper, stamps, laundry, and trolley fare.  Personal remarks and amorous references are written in code, several of which refer to Rizal's fiancée at that time, Leonor Rivera.  In his entries of June 5-30, Rizal notes his university exams in Greek, Latin, history, and medicine.  His last two entries, for Nov. 1 and 2, describe a farewell party for his friend, the painter Juan Luna, and Luna's departure for Paris.

desc: Primarily correspondence, memoranda, reports, and notes regarding Merrill's professional responsibilities (1888-1918). Also family and personal correspondence (1888-1911). Chronological files (1888-1912) contain correspondence on Newberry affairs, Chicago library activities (e.g. Chicago Library Club, Bibliographical Society of Chicago), classification, ALA issues, the Centre for University Extension, Catholicism, and family matters. This file ceases in 1919 when Merrill moved to public services.  There is also correspondence regarding ALA periodical cards and Merrill's  reminiscences of William Frederick Poole.  Correspondents include John Vance Cheney, George Watson Cole, Charles A. Cutter, Charles Martel, Carl B. Roden, Ellen Gates Starr, and George E. Wire.

title: Agenda de bufete o libro de memoria diario para 1884 con noticias y guia de Madrid.
creator: Rizal, José, 1861-1896.$$QRizal, José
desc: Printed diary for 1884, with handwritten entries for 1 Jan.-1 Nov. made by José Rizal as a twenty-three year-old student of art and medicine in Madrid. The entries contain Rizal's descriptions of his meetings in the cafés of Madrid with friends such as the Paterno brothers, Esteban Villanueva, Graciano López Jaena, Eduardo de Lete, and Valentín Ventura; his medical classes at the University and drawing classes at the Academia de San Fernando, as well as student strikes and protests; outings to the theatre; and references to political topics.  There are frequent references to the "Círculo", a society of Filipino residents of Madrid, founded in 1882, whose publication, "Revista del Círculo Hispano-Filipino" was strongly anti-Spanish. In addition, Rizal mentions books by Horace, Dumas, Voltaire, and Eugenio Sue--El judío errante--and records his daily expenditures for items such as food, paper, stamps, laundry, and trolley fare.  Personal remarks and amorous references are written in code, several of which refer to Rizal's fiancée at that time, Leonor Rivera.  In his entries of June 5-30, Rizal notes his university exams in Greek, Latin, history, and medicine.  His last two entries, for Nov. 1 and 2, describe a farewell party for his friend, the painter Juan Luna, and Luna's departure for Paris.

title: Indice di scritture che sono nell'Archivio vaticano segreto [Rome, ca. 1669].
creator: Archivio vaticano.$$QArchivio vaticano.
desc: Compilation, probably done in Rome around 1669, of indices of manuscripts from the Archivio vaticano segreto, one of the archives of the Biblioteca vaticana containing material dealing with matters of state. The ms. contains several different indices: the first (leaves [2]-[51]) lists the archival material alphabetically according to subject, from "Aqua putrida" to "Vallis montiones." Leaves [52]-[58], entitled "Extravagantes summorum Pontificum non impressae," contain a chronological list of the bulls preserved in manuscript form issued by popes from Innocence VI to Julius II.  An index of material dealing with the relations of the Papacy with foreign states--a miscellaneous collection of briefs, letters, instructions, relations, notes, speeches, and treatises taken from 17 v. marked "A"-"S", appears on leaves [59]-[118]. "Indice di nove volumi di M. Monterentii [Bishop Giulio Monterenzio?] segnati a tergo con lettere grandi ABCDEFGHI ... 1669" (leaves [119]-[166]) lists materials and cross-references for 9 v. of Monterenzio material. Finally, leaves [167]-[230], "Index scripturarum [con] existentium in Castro Sancti Angeli in camera thesaurari," contain an index of manuscript privileges and letters housed in the Castel Sant'Angelo in Rome, compiled by the Florentine Dominican, Father Zanobi Acciaiuolo, and issued under Leo X (1513-1521). Material is divided by subject area, and by location in white or colored linen bags.

desc: Photostatic reproduction of the text of the "Ganoda" chant of the Little Water Medicine Society of the Seneca Indians, probably transcribed by John Jacket, descendant of the Seneca chief Red Jacket, and chief singer of the "Pleasant Valley" lodge of the Society at Cattaraugus, N.Y.. One of the most important and best organized secret societies of the Seneca Indians was the Little Water Medicine Society, the ritual ceremonies of which were held on the fifth night of the new moon four times a year, to preserve the potency of the "secret medicine," or "niganĕga'á'", medicine bundles deposited by each member on the Altar of the Mystery. Members were persons for whom the ritual had been performed during sickness, or in response to dreams about the society.  The ms. includes the text of the chants arranged in numbered stanzas, as well as various notations on the money contributions made by members of the Society between 1849 and 1851.  There are scattered monetary entries throughout, the last one dated Sept. 14, 1870.

title: John B. Fithian papers.
creator: Fithian, John B., creator.$$QFithian, John B.
desc: Papers relating to John B. Fithian, a Civil War veteran and judge in the Probate Court of Will County. The materials consist of papers pertaining to Fithian's service during the Civil War, including a hand-written note, by John A. Rawlins, authorizing a pass for John Fithian and one pony from Vicksburg, Missississippi to Memphis, Tennessee and a handwritten note, dated October 24, 1865, ordering John Fithian to report for duty. In addition to the war era documents are several certificates and legal documents, including a certificate of membership for the Masonic Veteran Association of Illinois (1897); a document certifying Fithian as District Deputy Grand Master of the Eighth Masonic District (1902); and a certificate announcing the election of John B. Fithian as Judge of the Probate Court of Will Country signed by Governor Charles S. Deneen (1906); Stock certificate for 100 shares of the Sargent Cigar and Plantation Company (1911). Also included is a document from Cushing Development Company noting Fithian's purchase of property on an oil sub-division in Oklahoma. Also included are memorial material pertaining to Edna Whitake Fithian, the wife of John Fithian. These include a In Memoriam program, one photograph, and two obituaries.

title: [Letters] 1796 Oct. 17-1820 May 25.
creator: Blanckley, Henry Stanyford, d. 1820.$$QBlanckley, Henry Stanyford
desc: Letters, dated Oct. 17, 1796-May 25, 1820, written by and to Brevet-Major Henry Stanyford Blanckley, concerning his military career, especially his service as a military spy for the Duke of Wellington during the Peninsular War in Spain. The earliest letter, dated Oct. 17, 1796, is a note from the Foreign Secretary Sir William Grenville, agreeing to a meeting with Blanckley.  Blanckley's report of March 9, 1803 to Lords Hawkesbury [Earl of Liverpool] and St. Vincent documents his intelligence findings on French ship-building activities at the arsenal in Toulon, his arrest, and narrow escape to Marseilles. Blanckley spends some time in Nova Scotia, but when he hears of the Peninsular campaign, he writes to the commander-in-chief to request a return to Europe to serve with the army in Spain. His services in Spain are summarized in two reports: one entitled "Diario de noticias de los movimientos de los enemigos..." documents his spying between Dec. 1812 and May 1813; the other is an "Account of the strategems at Truxillo against General Foy after the taking of Badajoz", the text of which has been copied into a small black pocket notebook by Blanckley's nephew/niece.  Most of the other items are are Blanckley's letters, written between 1813 and 1818, to high-ranking officials such as Lord Fitzroy Somerset, the Duke of Wellington, Sir Henry Torrens, Lord Rowland Hill, Sir Benjamin Bloomfield, Sir Edward Pakenham, Sir John Sherbrooke, Sir Edward Barnes, and Lord Robert Castlereagh,

title: [Letter] [Palazzo] Pitti [Florence, Italy], to Benedetto Guerrini, 1643 Mar. 12.
creator: Dudley, Robert, Sir, 1574-1649.$$QDudley, Robert
desc: Autograph signed letter, dated March 12, 1643 at the Pitti Palace in Florence, from Robert Dudley, duke of Northumberland, to Benedetto Guerrini, chamberlain to the Grand Duke Ferdinand de' Medici II--to whom the work was eventually dedicated--relating to delays in the publication of Dudley's great sea atlas, the Arcano del mare (1646-1647). Although the Grand Duke authorized the printing more than eight months ago, only three half sheets have been printed so far.  Dudley has complained constantly about the delay, and Lucini, the engraver, is now in Florence trying to find out what the problem is.  Apparently, the printer blames the publisher, Francesco Rondinelli, a busy man, but also one who refuses any help with the atlas project. Dudley's friend, Evangelista Torricelli, mathematician and brilliant disciple of Galileo, has offered to help correct the proofs, but Rondinelli  has refused.  Dudley asks Guerrini to investigate the long delay, to talk to Lucini, and to ask the Grand Duke to expedite the project, or it will never be finished.

desc: Transcript of a mediation between General Robert Van Rensselaer and the chiefs of the Oneida Nation regarding a wampum belt found on an Oneida Indian during the American Revolutionary War. The wampum belt represented an alliance with the British against the American colonists. In the document, Van Rensselaer poses questions to the Oneida chiefs, who had been allied with the American colonists, regarding the intention of the belt and who had given it to the member of their tribe. Van Rensselaer imprisoned the suspected spy until he could be tried and, if found guilty, executed.

title: Histoire amoureuse d'Arenid et d'Heloise : Iere. partie : manuscript.
creator: Newberry Library. Manuscript. Case MS 5473.$$QNewberry Library.
desc: Unpublished love story and epistolary novel centered on the characters Arenid and Heloise, whom the former wishes to marry against the protests of his parents. Although never published, the manuscript is formatted similarly to a published book. The title page includes an edition statement ("Nouuelle edition"), a monogram vignette (possibly "AHLD"?) executed in gold leaf, and a mock imprint reading: A l'isle d'Amour, chez Constance la Tendre, rue de la Fidelité a l'Esperance, auec priuilege de Cupidon, M.D.C.X.VII. The preliminary matter ends with a parody of an "Approbation," dated 15 May 1697 and signed "Grand Secret, souuerain pontife de l'isle d'Amour"; "Extrait du priuillege de Cupidon," also dated 15 May 1697; and, rather than the printing privlege that would be common in published books of the time, a handwriting privilege ("acheué d'ecrire pour la premiere fois le 30e juillet 1697"). The monogram vignette on the title page is repeated, at a larger scale and also in gold leaf, on the last preliminary page. At the beginning of the volume is a full-page watercolor of a bouquet of flowers.

title: Robert and Elizabeth Barrett Browning letters, approximately 1849-1863.
creator: Browning, Robert, 1812-1889, correspondent.$$QBrowning, Robert
desc: Contains two letters, one written by Robert Browning and one by Elizabeth Barrett Browning composed between apporximately 1849-1863. The first letter written by Elizabeth Barrett Browning is addressed to "my dearest mona nina," referring to her friend Anna Jameson. The letter was written between 1849-1860. Elizabeth discusses that love equals correspondences, she wishes it would be summer soon, but she is not walking yet. Elizabeth briefly mentions Robert's father and asks Anna to keep the contents of this letter a secret because she does not want Robert to think she thinks differently. Elizabeth mentions Pen is doing well and is a "mamma's boy." The letter written by Robert Browning was written during his stay in Paris with Pen on March 27, 1863. Throughout the letter, Robert reacts to a "cheating manifestation" that his friend has witnessed. Robert does not believe one syllable of the explanation and believes that the "paper" is a forgery. He says that his friend's manifestation was brought on by a woman whose plan was to lead him astray, mainly because he valued her and lacked common sense. Robert asks that they do not ask him to testify on this topic. Robert discusses that Pen is healthy and growing. He briefly mentions he is working on a new edition of his works.

Manuscript. Case MS 5204.$$QNewberry Library.
desc: Seventeenth-century ms. copy from Béziers, France of the proceedings of a secret investigation into the vandalism of five parish churches in the town, and the subsequent destruction of church furnishings and religious relics by groups of Huguenots in 1562 and 1563. At the request of the local clergymen, the inquest was undertaken by the vicomte de Joyeuse, lieutenant-general of Languedoc, and the royal notary whom he deputized to assist him, Barthélemy Oisset, in order to assess the damage, and to identify the guilty parties.  The proceedings, held in Narbonne between Oct. 18-23, 1563, were transcribed by Thérosant Bernard, "praticien en Narbonne", and contain depositions of numerous witnesses, including Anthoine Pradel of Rouergue, who testified that a large mob of Huguenots, armed with rapiers, daggers, halbeards, and pistols, forced its way into the parish churches of St. Nazaire, St. Afrodise, St. Jacques, St. Felix, and Ste. Magdelaine, tearing down velvet and silken draperies, defacing holy relics, and stealing silver chalices, candelabra, and altarpieces.  Religious statues and crucifixes were hauled into the streets, and set afire. Apparently a second contemporary copy was made from the original by notary Jean Vitalis. An added note at the end states that the text was later copied from the chapter archives of St. Nazaire in Béziers by notary and chapter secretary, De Rocoles.

title: Letter Manila, to Diego Feri de Nalda, 1684 June 8.
creator: Calderón y Serrano, Diego, d. 1687.$$QCalderón y Serrano, Diego
desc: Letter, dated June 8, 1684 in Manila, from Diego Calderón y Serrano, oidor of the Manila Audiencia, to Diego Feri de Nalda, concerning the estate of the late Francisco de Coloma y Maceda. Calderón reports on the turmoil in Manila which resulted when the Audiencia judges exiled the archbishop, Felipe Pardo; and refers to scandalous attacks against the Audiencia by the Dominicans who defended the archbishop, as he is a member of their own order. Because of the turmoil, Father Juan de Santa María declined to serve as executor for the estate of Coloma, former oidor of the Audiencia who died in 1677, and Calderón appointed Capt. Francisco González Zorrilla as "tenedor de bienes."  It has been difficult for Father Santa María to organize Coloma's financial dealings, and the little money he has left at his disposal will be used to cover the expenses of withdrawing the 12,000 pesos from Coloma's accounts in the royal treasury. Hopefully the situation will improve with the arrival of the galleon from New Spain in July.  In response to an inquiry from the marqués de Canales concerning his uncle's possible dealings with the Jesuits, Calderón says that he cannot help, as the records are very confusing.  He suggests that should Feri de Nalda find himself in Mexico City, he should contact Fray Nicolás de Merlo there who may have access to some secret book of accounts.

title: Diaries 1858 Jan. 1-1866 Dec. 31.
creator: Wing, John M. (John Mansir), 1845-1917.$$QWing, John M.
desc: Nine pocket diaries containing entries by book collector and newspaperman, John M. Wing, for the years 1858 to 1866. Wing was an avid journal writer, almost unfailingly making an entry for each day of the year in his diary which he considered to be "a useful book", "the best companion that adversity gives", "a true friend, a secret counselor".  He began keeping a diary in 1858, when he was only thirteen years old, and the early journals from 1858-1862 contain his observations on weather, dinners and meetings with friends, classes and homework assignments at the Pulaski Academy in Pulaski, N.Y. where he was a student, and his experiences setting type and working in the print shop of the Pulaski Democrat. The diaries also contain miscellaneous quotes jotted down from Latin authors, Shakespeare, and other poets; for example, the 1861 diary begins with a patriotic Civil War poem (by Wing?) attacking "Jeff Davis" and the "traitors" who need to be taught to "obey the Constitution", and ends with Wing's pen sketch of Davis on the gallows. In addition, the 1862 and 1863 diaries contain a small pocket in which Wing kept numerous small newspaper clippings of interest, collection receipts, business cards, and short pencilled notes. Beginning in 1863, as Wing continued his newspaper career in the Rome office of the Utica Evening Telegraph, the entries became progressively longer and more detailed, and often included Wing's accounts of his newspaper subscription collections. desc: Photostatic copies of documents concerning Innes' legal, political, and financial dealings in Virginia and Kentucky between 1784 and 1808. James Wilkinson. Box 4 contains correspondence relating to the legal disputes between Innes and Humphrey Marshall. Box 2 contains correspondence between Innes and Henry Knox, War Dept. Secretary, concerning the use of militia and scouts to defend the western frontier of Virginia along the Ohio River from hostile Indians; a memo and map defining boundaries of Cherokee land, established in a 1791 treaty; as well as letters from other correspondents such as John Brown, Virginia governor Beverly Randolph, and Gen. title: Report on salt mines in Mexico, 1857 November 2 : manuscript.
creator: Ledo, Octaviano Muñoz, 1815-1874, author.$$QLedo, Octaviano Muñoz
desc: Report describes the reformation of the salt mining code in Mexico, including a 26 article bill regarding the splattering of salt mines. Report examines salt mines on private properties and determines in salt mines located on private property belong to the owner of the land and those owners should be compensated when salt is extracted from their land. The report also indicates proposed changes to the mining rules because of the importance of salt mines to Mexico and to ensure the safety and management of salt mining companies. The report also references the history of mining in France. The salt mine, Peñón Blanco in San Luis Potosí is referenced throughout the report.

title: Apuntes informes sobre Filipinas.
creator: Vindel, Pedro.$$QVindel, Pedro. | Edward E. Ayer Manuscript Collection (Newberry Library)$$QEdward E. Ayer Manuscript Collection (Newberry Library) | Newberry Library. Manuscript. Ayer MS 1297.$$QNewberry Library.
desc: Series of unsigned, undated reading notes on various topics pertaining to the Philippines, probably written around 1853. There are references to voyages of scientific observation and hydrographic surveying, and particular mention of the discovery of the Philippines by Magellan, and the expedition of Alessandro Malaspina of 1789-1794.  Other notes discuss the Spanish conquest of the islands, and present the views of Apodaca (possibly naval commander José Ruiz de Apodaca) on the layout of the port of Manila in Manila Bay, and changes made by the English.  A list of works to consult contains such titles as "Diccionario de las Islas Filipinas;" "Quince años en las Islas Filipinas;" and Jacque Arago's Souvenirs d'un aveugle: voyage autour du monde;" as well as references to authors such as Quesada, Morata, and Antonio Saavedra.  The author of the notes includes page numbers from the sources he has consulted.

title: [Notarial cartulary for the Confraternity of the Cross in Ferrara, Italy], 1530-1586.
creator: Newberry Library. Manuscript. Case MS 5321.$$QNewberry Library.
desc: Notarial cartulary, transcribed for--and probably at--the Confraternity of the Cross in Ferrara, Italy, containing 15 documents, dated between 1530 and 1586. The documents in the register deal with donations and indulgences of the Confraternity over a period of approximately eighty years, each one witnessed by a notary, whose cipher and initials appear in the margins, next to the traditional notarial oath which begins "Ego..." Included are indulgences; copy, dated Jan. 15, 1530, of a bull by Pope Clement VII concerning the Confraternity's charter; a copy of the will of one of the Confraternity members, Father Constantino Cardano, an inventory of his property, and a memo on the execution of his will; a memo on the bequest of Domenico Bondio to the Confraternity; absolutions granted to various persons by the Confraternity; and a memo about the Confraternity's relic--a piece of wood from the Cross--and the order to make a copy in silver.

title: Garrett A. Boge collection of inscriptional rubbings, 1991-2007.
creator: Boge, Garrett A., creator.$$QBoge, Garrett A.
desc: Consists of 343 rubbings from 296 stones inscribed with symbols or texts, primarily in Rome and Florence, which Garrett Boge made between 1991 and 2007. Initially the rubbings served for his research into historical letterforms and they were used as models for type faces he designed and marketed. As he honed his technique, he moved beyond the original documentary impulse to create art works of considerable beauty which have been exhibited and collected by others. The collection has two general themes: Roman capital letterforms (from Roman Republican through Neoclassical periods) on stones in Rome, Florence and elsewhere; and early Christian symbols (primarily birds) from third- to fifth-century tomb fragments housed in the Vatican epigraphy collection and in churches in Rome.

desc: Ms. copy, dated Oct. 24, 1717 in Faenza, Italy, of Raoul-Auger Feuillet's Chorégraphie, translated into Italian by Carlo Cesare Scaletta. Feuillet's innovative system of dance notation, popular in Europe throughout the 18th century, replaced verbal description with symbols to notate the dancer's steps and floor patterns. Topics discussed and diagrammed include the dancer's posture and manner of walking; dance positions and their variations; explanation of how to interpret the symbols used in diagramming the dance movements; and dance tempos and rhythms.  There is also a chapter containing Feuillet notation of commonly-used dance steps such as the "galiarda", "coppé" and "mezzo coppé", "bourée", or "fleuret"; "jetée"; "chassée", "sissonne", and "piroüette."  A supplementary final chapter, entitled "Agiunta d'alcuni balli per mostrare in pratticha  quanto per l'adietro si è insegnato", presents floor diagrams and music for the various segments of the dance, "La Bourgogne": "entrata à due", "courante", "borea", "sarabanda", and "passe pied".

desc: Photostatic reproduction of a French-Miami Illinois dictionary and devotional texts in Illinois, compiled by Jean Baptiste Le Boulanger, possibly during the 1730s. The dictionary occupies 180 leaves, and lists approximately 3,000 words in French, from "abbaisser" to "vuider," followed by equivalents in Illinois.  Devotional materials include prayers and a catechism in Illinois; explanations of the Ten Commandments and the symbols of the Apostles; translations of readings for the church year from the Gospels; and a translation of the Book of Genesis.  There are also three pages of verb conjugations in Illinois.

title: Essential and invisible the goddess of the hearth.
creator: Berry, Jill K.$$QBerry, Jill K.
desc: Calligraphic book in acrylic, watercolor, gouache, and foil, written and designed by Jill K. Berry in celebration of Vesta, the Roman goddess of the hearth, and metaphor for motherhood, and for all women/mothers everywhere who tend to be "invisible and essential." Text lines in a small uncial hand, inspired by the Homeric hymns, are interspersed with lines in a large cursive hand, from the Italian "Prayer of a vestal," and are scripted in violet and white inks on Arches Text Wove paper colored in mixed tones of light ultramarine blue, gold, and violet. Each of the uncial texts is preceded by a small gold foil symbol, taken from both modern and ancient sources, and associated with the theme of women and motherhood, such as "heart and windpipe", "fire", "house", "festival", and "homecoming". Verso of last leaf contains the universal symbol for "woman", composed of a fabric of strips of colored paper partially woven together, over which is sewn a set of spiralling circles in copper foil thread. Cf. artist's description of ms. on laid-in leaf.

title: Copied diary of bicycle trip, July 7 to Aug. 30, '99 1899 Sept. 10.
creator: Wildes, F.C.$$QWildes, F.C.
desc: Ms. diary, copied in Sept. 1899 by F.C. Wildes from his original papers, on his return from a bicycle tour which he and his wife, Kate, undertook from Fort Dodge, Iowa between July 7 and Aug. 30, 1899. Journal entries describe the route, road conditions, hotels and private homes where they stay, people they encounter, and train and steamer travel, as the Wildes make their way through back-roads and small towns in Iowa, Minnesota, Wisconsin, and Illinois. Some of the places they visit include Badger, Humboldt, Algona, Bancroft, and Elmore in Iowa; Amboy, Vernon City, Garden City, Mankato, Lake Washington, Waterville, Morristown, Minnehaha, Minneapolis, St. Paul, and Wayzata in Minnesota; Bayfield, Stevens Point, Amherst, Sheridan, Neenah, Menasha, Oshkosh, Shebohygan, and Milwaukee in Wisconsin; and Chicago, Melrose, Elgin, and Rockford in Illinois.  They return via East Dubuque and Independence to Fort Dodge, where Wildes is a schoolteacher.  Although the bicycle tour ends on Aug. 30, the journal includes a few later entries from Aug. 31, Sept. 9--Wildes receives news of the sudden death of Eugene Wildes of Bath, Maine--and Sept. 10, when Wildes "just finished writing up this diary from the first page of this book (the one from which this book was copied)."

creator: Waldeck, Frédéric de, 1766-1875.$$QWaldeck, Frédéric de
desc: Volume 25 of Waldeck's notebooks, containing comments and observations on topics pertaining to Aztec and Mayan culture, compiled in 1834 in preparation for his upcoming trip to the Yucatan, with additions and corrections from 1835-1837. There are brief notes on subjects such as taxidermy, the compass, migration theories explaining the Asian characteristics of the Aztecs and Toltecs, symbolic animals and colors, and masques. Waldeck discusses Aztec language and hieroglyphics, their similarities with Egyptian symbols, and their appearance in various codexes; and explains various Aztec deities, providing lists of their Greek counterparts, a genealogical table of the gods (p. [62]), and sketches.  He comments at length on Juarros' study of Guatemala, and critiques the theories of Baron von Humboldt throughout. Also included are sections on Indian physionomy, sacrifices, feather art, sculpture and architecture.

desc: Deck of 52 playing cards repurposed as a manuscript card catalog, written in at least two hands, for a library or collection of French books, most of which were published between 1649 and 1812. On the verso of each card is an entry for one book, which includes shelfmark, title, author, place and date of publication, number of volumes, and bibliographic format or size. The format of the entries conforms to guidelines published in an early manual for systematizing catalog cards for libraries and book collections, Instruction pour procéder à la confection du catalogue de chacune des bibliothèques sur lesquelles les directoires ont dû ou doivent incessament apposer les scellés (Paris : De l'Imprimerie nationale, 1791), which recommends the use of repurposed playing cards. The cataloged books include histories, treatises, and works of literature. The playing cards where made by Parisian card maker Jean Minot, whose name "Minot" is printed on the Queen of Spades. Woodcut figures are printed on the face cards and hand colored with stencils; the numeral cards are stenciled with the symbols of their respective suits.

title: [Certification of the arms of Juan Ramón de Torres Bermúdez of Cádiz], 1788 Sept. 25.
creator: Rújula, Juan Félix de, 1744-1806.$$QRújula, Juan Félix de
desc: Certification of the arms of Juan Ramón de Torres Bermúdez of Cádiz by official chronicler Juan Félix de Rújula, dated Sept. 25, 1788 in Madrid. Torres Bermúdez, whose confirmation of nobility status or "hidalguía" was recently issued by the Alcaldes de la Sala de Hijos-Dalgo in Granada on June 18, 1788, has requested an examination, description, and certification of his family arms, all of which are contained in the ms. prepared by Rújula.  Each of the four main branches of Torres' ancestry has its roots in Galicia--the Torres and Bermúdez lines on his father's side, and the Cobelo and Puga families on his mother's side--and is described separately, with notes on family history and names and exploits of important family members, location of ancestral estates, and description of their respective arms.  Verso of leaf [22] begins a brief genealogy of Torres himself, going back four generations.  Rújula explains the heraldic colors and symbols of the Torres Bermúdez composite arms, and, with his signature, affixes an embossed paper seal.  Below are additional seals and certifications of Sept. 26, 1788, signed by the royal scribes of Madrid, and by Manuel de Pinedo of the Order of Carlos III, former secretary of the king's council and municipal official.

desc: Deeds, wills, and a map in Nahuatl and Spanish from 1678-1781, relating to the sale and inheritance of property in San Pedro de Calimaya in the Toluca Valley, and Teocaltitlán, a barrio of Mexico City. The Teocaltitlán documents, dated 1678-1748, pertain to a parcel of land owned by Juan de la Cruz and his wife María de los Angeles, both Indians.  The pictorial plan of their house and property contains symbols and text in Nahuatl, and indicates the measurements of the lot.  Their wills in both Nahuatl and Spanish, specify the disposition of the property; María's will is dated June 12, 1701, while Juan's is dated June 6, 1725.  There are also three deeds from 1678 to property in Teocaltitlán; two bills of sale for land in the barrio; and finally, the will of Francisca de los Angeles, dated June 22, 1748.  The remaining seven documents, dated 1738-1781, consist of deeds for parcels of land in San Pedro de Calimaya belonging to Juan de Dios, and Antonio de Santiago and his wife Andrea Antonía; and the wills of Felix de Santiago, Pascuala de la Cruz, and Martina María, each bearing reference to various properties in Calimaya.  Five of these documents are in Nahuatl, with official translations into Spanish of two of them, dated Nov. 21, 1772.

title: Papers, 1825-1867.
creator: Waldeck, Frédéric de, 1766-1875.$$QWaldeck, Frédéric de
desc: Waldeck's notes, sketches, letters, and a catalog of drawings, dating from 1825-1867 and relating to his travels in Mexico, his ideas on the origins, history, and culture of the Indians of Mexico, and his collection of drawings of the ruins and antiquities of Palenque and other sites in the Yucatan peninsula. The bulk of the collection are Waldeck's notes, most of which were intended for his never-published Encyclopédie archéologique, a comprehensive encyclopedia of Mexican antiquities which he was preparing during the years 1829-1832.  They describe the layout at such sites as Palenque, Ocozinco, Labna, Tulum, Xochicalco, Teotihuacan, and Mayapán; the architecture, sculpture, and painting of the monuments, and the significance of certain gods, symbols and colors.  Other topics include the Indian calendar, hieroglyphics, possible links with ancient cultures of India and Egypt, social customs, and natural history.  Some notes comment on works by other authors, especially Stephens and Catherwood's Incidents of travel, and Del Rio's report of early excavations at Palenque.  In addition, Waldeck discusses his own published works: Voyage pittoresque (1838) and his Palenque drawings, Monuments anciens du Mexique (1866).  There is also a sketchbook containing landscapes, Indian motifs, and plans, and a small catalog of 129 drawings of Indian gods and dress.

title: Journal de notes no. 1 relevées des différens ouvrages que j'ai le temps de lire entre mes autres occupations. par renvoy de numéro  / Waldeck.
creator: Waldeck, Frédéric de, 1766-1875.$$QWaldeck, Frédéric de
desc: Waldeck's notebook for his never-realized project the Encyclopédie archéologique, compiled between 1860 and 1866, after he had returned to Paris, contains notes and reflections on the history and culture of the Indians of Mexico, with particular emphasis on the Mayan civilization of Palenque. Many of Waldeck's notes deal with the possibility of Chinese and Japanese influences on the development of Indian writing and sculpture in Mexico.  He also discusses the construction, measurements, and meaning of the pyramids at Teotihuacán, Xochicalco, Palenque, and Cholula.  Other frequently-mentioned subjects deal with symbols such as the quetzal bird in art and sculpture; the significance of the Indian gods; architectural descriptions of ruins throughout the Yucatán; the migration of Asiatic peoples to the Yucatán; and the physionomy of the Indians.  Waldeck includes his reactions to two London newspaper articles of 1866, excerpts of which he has copied into his notebook; and throughout, jots down comments on his readings of authors such as Stephens, Winkelman, von Humboldt, and de Landa, with a special critique of Abbé Brasseur's Histoire des nations civilisées.  Finally, in a note from April 1864, Waldeck sees his published works--the 1838 Voyage pittoresque and Monuments anciens du Mexique, his Palenque drawings which were eventually published in 1866--as important studies of a little-known area of history; and discusses plans for a third work.

title: Catalogue des dessins Mexico, 1829 June-1831 October.
creator: Waldeck, Frédéric de, 1766-1875.$$QWaldeck, Frédéric de
desc: Waldeck's own descriptive catalog from June 1829, with additional notes and entries from 1830 and 1831, covering drawings he either created or acquired in Mexico between 1825 and 1831 of ancient and modern Indian subjects, their native dress, daily life, architecture, and sculptures. According to Waldeck, the drawings were made from documents at the University of Mexico, and from items held by private collectors such as Greaves and Uhde and by Waldeck himself. He describes his drawings of Mexican warriors, gods, and rulers, based on painted manuscripts or on sculpted basalt or terra cotta figures; drawings of ancient Indians from different social classes with detailed descriptions of their clothing and adornments; drawings of modern Indians--mine workers, water carriers, and tortilla makers--from such villages as Tamaulipas and Santa Catalina; landscapes; and drawings of masks, vases, sculpted symbols, and calendar wheels.  Waldeck also includes an inventory of his own collection of original Indian pictorial manuscripts (some of which are catalogued separately as Ayer Mss. 1900, 1902, 1903, 1904, and 1907).  Entries indicate the collection numbers assigned by Waldeck, with corresponding plate numbers.

title: [Autograph album] Chemawa (Salem, Or.), 1888-1911.
creator: Amera, Charles, 1870-1897.$$QAmera, Charles
desc: Autograph album belonging to Nez Percé Indian Charles Amera, containing notes and signatures of fellow students and teachers on the occasion of graduation day at the Chemawa Indian School, with most entries dated June and July 1888. Charles Amera, born on White Bird Creek, Idaho, on Dec. 25, 1870, was one of many Nez Percé Indians sent to the Chemawa Indian School in Salem, Oregon, where he was also known as Caleb Charles. This is his graduation autograph album with inscriptions from both male and female classmates, some of them Nez Percé, and related to Amera, others from different reservations in Oregon, such as Umatilla, Klamath , Grand Ronde, and Warm Springs.  All entries include date and writer's full name, as well as school identification number.  On blank pages, Amera has added personal information, including a transcription of his honorable discharge from the army, where he served as trumpeter in Troop "L" of the 4th U.S. Cavalry Regiment from Sept. 28, 1892-Aug. 2, 1893 at Fort Walla Walla in Washington. Later entries in different hands include death dates of some of the students mentioned, including a note under Amera's name: "Died Jan. 1897." An entire page is devoted to the death and burial dates of 11 people who died between Dec. 1910 and March 1911, apparently as a result of one of the frequent epidemics to hit the reservation in the early 1900s.  Names of the deceased include Sarah Hines, Cornelius Lookingglass, George Moses, Dick Moses, Corbett Frank, Thom

desc: Bound collection of documents regarding the sale of lands owned by Indigenous peoples in Tlaxcala and Puebla, Mexico. Many sales involve the transfer of communal lands of Indigenous towns to outsiders. In many instances, the collection documents the cultural practices that Indigenous Mexican people engaged in when buying and selling property. The first volume traces the ownership of the hacienda of San Juan Mixco in Tlaxcala from 1719 to 1823 and includes documents concerning an attempt by two caciques, or Indigenous leaders, from Ocotelulco to recover land from the hacienda and disputes between the Spanish family who owned the hacienda and Indigenous people in the nearby town of Santa Apolonia over the rights to an aqueduct. This volume concludes with a suit brought against the hacienda's owner in the 1820s by the Indigenous people of San Damián, who were attempting to claim some of the hacienda's land after the owner had fallen into debt. Included is a richly illustrated manuscript map (53 x 74 cm) of the hacienda of San Juan Mixco and the surrounding towns commissioned by the Indigenous people of San Damián and drawn by Antonio de Santa María Incháurregui, architect of Puebla, in 1809 ("Plano corografico que demuéstra la figura que forman las tierras comprehende la hazienda nombrada San Juan Mixco, en jurisdiccion y doctrina del pueblo de Santa Maria Nativitas"). title: Journal de poche de Natchan / J.F. Waldeck : nottes [!] de théogonie azteque et variété d'autres, pour servir en voyage. Palenque. No. 24 (Treis).
creator: Waldeck, Frédéric de, 1766-1875.$$QWaldeck, Frédéric de
desc: Waldeck's pocket journal, dating from March 1832 to August 1853, containing his notes on the Aztec deities and other miscellaneous historical and cultural topics. Waldeck begins with a list of authors consulted--among them Boturini, Acosta, Clavigero, Sahagún, Díaz del Castillo and Thévénot--indicating that he had read many of the important works on Indian civilization.  He goes on to describe each Aztec deity, analyzing the name, counterpart in Greek mythology, area of domain, and symbols.  He also includes reflections on a variety of topics such as theories of Phoenician migration to the Yucatán, the invention of the compass, the Aztec calendar, masques, symbolic uses of color, and werewolves.  Notes from London, 1853, include a comment on Stephen's Incidents of travel in Chiapas, and a critique of methods used by Stephens and his illustrator Frederick Catherwood to study Aztec painting.  He also offers an 1853 transcription of earlier notes damaged in a chimney fire, concerning the history of Palenque (Natchan) and the ruins there.  With the journal is a small gold tin box (130 x 90 mm.) from a Paris pharmacy,  which once contained mustard plasters, used by Waldeck to hold a collection of 37 "flashcards."  Waldeck apparently cut up some lithographic prints,  by Beer, and by Lemercier, Benard, et Cie. (first established in Paris in 1837), and created a series of 37 small cards (60 x 110 mm.) each containing a Nahuatl vocabulary term, or a small pen or pencil outline dr

title: Plan géometrîque et declaration des domaines du Chaigne Paroisse de Boyer appartenants a Dame Jeanne De Toisy, veuve du Sieur François Seriziat, négotiant, résidante en la Ville de Lyon / [1790]. / levé por Philibert Petit, Commissaire aux Rentes Emphitéoliques, résidant a Senecey le Chateau en 1790,
creator: Petit, Philibert.$$QPetit, Philibert.
desc: Ornately-calligraphed ms. land-use survey of 1790 of the estate of Jeanne De Toisy, widow of François Seriziat, located between Tournus and Chalon near Sennecey in Burgundy. The ms., drawn and signed by Philibert Petit, the local Commissaire aux Rentes, describes and measures 195 "ouvrées" of vineyards (an "ouvrée" is the amount of land a man can cultivate in one day), as well as other cultivated and wooded properties. The maps, drawn to scale, are labeled with the names of the tenant farmers, and indicate roads and communal land ("finage") as well.  Facing pages contain explanatory notes, number and sizes of the parcels, and list of buildings located on the property. The document may have been intended to indicate the precise apportionment of the production between the owners and tenants, or to determine tax assessments on the estate.

desc: Correspondence, dated between Oct. 6, 1806 and Dec. 13, 1816, concerning the Burr Conspiracy of 1805-1807, and power struggles by the U.S., Britain, and Spain for control of Mexico, and the southeastern territories of East and West Florida and New Orleans. Box 1 begins with a letter from Presley Nevill and Samuel Roberts from Oct. 6, 1806, warning secretary of state James Madison of Burr's conspiracy.  Subsequent letters, many from New Orleans and Natchez, present views on Burr's treason and the trial at Richmond. Correspondents include Aaron Burr, his co-conspirator Harman Blennerhassett, James Madison, President Thomas Jefferson, General James A. Wilkinson, his aide-de-camp Walter Burling, William C.C. Claiborne, governor of Louisiana,  Robert Williams, governor of Mississippi territory, Judge Harry Toulmin, John Graham, Comfort Tyler, Horatio Stark, and C.A. Rodney. Box 2 contains additional Burr material, such as depositions and lists of witnesses, some from 1806 and 1808, but most undated. It also contains correspondence and papers concerning foreign relations between the U.S., Spain, and Britain, and the fears of the latter two countries of losing their colonial territories to American intrigues and aggression, specifically Louisiana, East and West Florida, and Mexico. desc: Ms., dated Aug. 1761, probably in [Lisbon?] Portugal [?], and signed by Antonio da Sylva e Faria, possibly the royal notary or scribe, containing instructions for the baptismal ceremony of the first-born son of Maria, Princess of Brazil (later Queen of Portugal), and her husband, the Infante D. title: [Poetry and prose] [between 1649 and 1666].
creator: Ciampoli, Giovanni Battista, 1590-1643.$$QCiampoli, Giovanni Battista
desc: Transcriptions of essays, poems, and letters by Giovanni Ciampoli, written in different hands on odd sheets of paper and unbound gatherings, brought together after Ciampoli's death, probably between 1649 and 1666. His religious poems include "Meditationi davidiche in tempo di calunnie"; "Meditatione sopra il Salmo 113"; "Hinno secondo in lode del Beato Luigi Gonzaga"; "Cantico delle benedittione", written for the coronation of Urban VIII in 1626; and "Coro musicale de i pastori di Bettelem nella notte di Natale". There is also an epic poem dedicated to Cardinal Francesco Barberini, "nel suo retorno delle due legationi di Francia e Spagna"; and other poems such as "La potenza repudiata: al Signor Don Carlo Bossio"; "Canzone in morte della Signora Contessa Livia d'Arco Ferrarere", "Canzone contro gl'invidiosi", and "Canzone al Signor Vicenzo Cappone, in lode della fatica". Prose pieces include an essay, "Discorso della mortificatione", and some of Ciampoli's correspondence with Cardinal Antonio Barberino and Cardinal Spada (1636), and King Władystaw IV of Poland (1638). Also included are an "argomento" for an epic poem on the Huns which Urban VIII proposed to write; hymns for Maddalena Cesi on the day on which she became a nun; two moral poems "Disprezzo della corte e delle ricchezze" and "Contro l'infedelta degl'amici in corte"; two musical dramas, "Le vendemmie di Castel Gandolfo" and 'Le nozze di Bacco e della Neve"; and a choral dialogue, "La ninfa del Peru".

desc: Documents, probably compiled by Jean Gratien de Laussat in France between 1771 and 1789, concerning the position of "réceveur-général des finances de Béarn and Navarre" which he had occupied since 1765. The kingdom of Navarre (Navarre and Béarn provinces, county of Foix, Bigorre, Nébouzan, 3 bastilles of Marsan, Cursan, and Gabardan, and 4 valleys of Aure, Magnas, Barousse, and Nestes) traditionally had two positions of "receveur-général des finances", one held by Jean Gratien de Laussat, the other by his colleague, Jean-Etienne de Péne. To reorganize and centralize accounting procedures under the French king, an Aug. 1772 edict abolishes Laussat's position, merges Péne's position with that of treasurer general of Navarre, and recommends that he be appointed to fill it. Vol. I contains correspondence (copies and originals), rough drafts of letters, petitions, position papers, and numerous memos, dated between 1771 and 1787, containing historical and legal precedents, and opinions of other tax officials and government lawyers in support of Laussat.  Also included is a table comparing revenues collected under the old and new systems.  Vol. 2 contains excerpts from some 13 "brevets des Etats Generaux de Béarn" from 1773-1785, signed by Ducos, secretary of state.  Printed items are bound in as well, including edicts from 1633-1784 on financial administration and tax collection in Navarre, and excerpts from the proceedings of the Parlement de Navarre. title: Genealogical chronicle of the Monroy family of Cáceres, Spain [ca. 1630]
creator: Maldonado, Alonso de, active 15th century. Hechos de don Alonso de Monroy.$$QMaldonado, Alonso de | Phillipps, Thomas, Sir, 1792-1872, former owner.$$QPhillipps, Thomas
desc: Unsigned, undated ms. chronicle, probably from Spain around 1630, containing the history and genealogy of the Monroy family of the Cáceres region of Spain. The chronicle begins with the reign of Clodio at the time of the birth of Christ, and describes how the Monroys are descended from the same family line as the kings of France.  It recounts the Mon[te]rroy family history of births, marriages, and death, and their military achievements in the service of the king--especially reclaiming territory from the Moors between 711 and the 15th century--for which they are rewarded with large tracts of land, enabling them to become important landowners and leaders of the Orden de Alcántara, a powerful military religious order in Spain. Important early family members include the brothers Nuño Pérez de Monrroy, abbot of Santander, and favorite of King Sancho III; and his brother, Fernán Pérez de Monrroy.  Several generations later, Hernán Pérez de Monrroy marries Doña Isabel de Almaraz, and has 4 sons: Diego, Alvaro, archdeacon of Guadalaxara and dean of the cathedral in Plasencia; Alonso, and Rodrigo.  For his victories over the Moors, Alonso becomes "clavero" and, eventually, "maestre" of the Order of Alcántara.

title: Indice di scritture che sono nell'Archivio vaticano segreto [Rome, ca. 1669].
creator: Archivio vaticano.$$QArchivio vaticano.
desc: Compilation, probably done in Rome around 1669, of indices of manuscripts from the Archivio vaticano segreto, one of the archives of the Biblioteca vaticana containing material dealing with matters of state. The ms. contains several different indices: the first (leaves [2]-[51]) lists the archival material alphabetically according to subject, from "Aqua putrida" to "Vallis montiones." Leaves [52]-[58], entitled "Extravagantes summorum Pontificum non impressae," contain a chronological list of the bulls preserved in manuscript form issued by popes from Innocence VI to Julius II.  An index of material dealing with the relations of the Papacy with foreign states--a miscellaneous collection of briefs, letters, instructions, relations, notes, speeches, and treatises taken from 17 v. marked "A"-"S", appears on leaves [59]-[118]. "Indice di nove volumi di M. Monterentii [Bishop Giulio Monterenzio?] segnati a tergo con lettere grandi ABCDEFGHI ... 1669" (leaves [119]-[166]) lists materials and cross-references for 9 v. of Monterenzio material. Finally, leaves [167]-[230], "Index scripturarum [con] existentium in Castro Sancti Angeli in camera thesaurari," contain an index of manuscript privileges and letters housed in the Castel Sant'Angelo in Rome, compiled by the Florentine Dominican, Father Zanobi Acciaiuolo, and issued under Leo X (1513-1521). Material is divided by subject area, and by location in white or colored linen bags.

title: Idea conversationis humana christiano-politica, seu, Philosophia moralis ad virtutum moralium et cultissima humanitatis normam efformata per breves tesseras expressa varijs hominum statibus ac conditionibus accommodata  / a R.P. Joanne Siminski, S.J.
creator: Siminski, Joannes, 1637-1700.$$QSiminski, Joannes
desc: Unsigned contemporary copy of a philosophical treatise on Christian behavior, written in Germany by the Jesuit Joannes Siminski, probably during the late 17th century. After a prologue and a section on the definition of ethics, the work is arranged by "tesserae," or "watchwords," which help the Christian to lead a moral and virtuous life.  Concepts discussed include friendship; honesty; love; fortitude; humor; strength to tolerate adversity; suffering; matrimonial love; and trust in God.  There is also a dialogue on Death between Reason (Ratio) and Feeling (Sensus).

title: [Guest register] 1837 June 16-1840 Sept. 29.
creator: Cataract House (Niagara Falls, N.Y.)$$QCataract House (Niagara Falls, N.Y.)
desc: Guest register of the Cataract House in Niagara Falls, N.Y., for June 16, 1837 to Sept. 29, 1840. The Cataract House, one of the early large hotels at Niagara Falls, was built by Parkhurst Whitney in 1832, and remained in operation until the 1920's.  The register contains the names of thousands of travellers to the Falls, their places of residence, room numbers, and destinations.  Guests hail from all parts of the United States, although many are residents of  towns nearby such as Lewiston, and Chippawa, and other New York cities such as Rochester, Oswego, Oneida, Rome, Binghamton, and Buffalo.  Massachusetts, Pennsylvania, New Jersey, and Connecticut are well-represented--there is even a group led by a professor from Yale University, and Canadians visit from Halifax and Toronto.  Many guests are American or British military officers, probably because of the Canadian Rebellion of 1837-1838, which resulted in a concentration of American military forces in Buffalo and Niagara Falls.  Scattered among the guests' names are brief notes on the schedules of steamships and packet boats which serve the Falls, including the "St. George", the "Oswego", and the "Syracuse."  Other notes record accidents at the Falls, such as the death of N.L. Hungerford of West Troy, "killed by the falling of stones at the Cave of the Winds"; or a fire aboard the steamboat "Washington" on June 16, 1838, in which 40 or 50 passengers were burnt or lost.

desc: Ms. copy, transcribed by an anonymous Italian, probably during the 18th-century, of Agrippa's Cabala angelica of 1517. The work is a treatise on numerology, and the occult meanings of numbers. The text is illustrated with tables and pyramids containing the months of the year and the numbers associated with each; the numerical values of each letter of the alphabet; and several tables of the "planetary alphabets".  Other tables explore the relationships of numbers to the days of the week, the hours of the day, the signs of the Zodiac, and the movements of the sun.

title: Letters Manila, to the Conde de Aranda, 1772 July 21-July 30.
creator: Philippines. Gobernador-General (1770-1776 : Anda y Salazar)$$QPhilippines. Gobernador-General (1770-1776 : Anda y Salazar)
desc: Three letters, dated July 21-30, 1772, from Simón de Anda, governor of the Philippines, to the Conde de Aranda, president of the Consejo de Castilla, and the moving force behind the expulsion of the Jesuits from Spanish territories, acknowledging various orders pertaining to the liquidation of Jesuit assets. Letter No. 1 responds to a royal order of Jan. 23, 1771, concerning liquidation of Jesuit temporalities, the secular revenues of the order; their deposit in the Royal Treasury; and the handling of charitable funds of the obras pías. Letter No. 3 discusses an order which concerns the remuneration of the lawyer charged with defending the Jesuit assets, and which points out that his duties are incompatible with the duties of those entrusted with administering the houses belonging to the temporalities.  Letter No. 7 acknowledges a royal order of Dec. 1, 1771 for the disposition of the gold and ornaments owned by French Jesuit missionaries to China and Pondicherry (India) which were included among the temporalities of the Philippine Jesuits.  Each letter promises prompt compliance.

creator: Bermejo, Julián, 1777-1851.$$QBermejo, Julián
desc: Ms. copy, possibly from around 1800, of a grammar of the Cebuano language, attributed to Julián Bermejo, based on the work of Padre Francisco Encina. The grammar begins with notes on the Cebuano alphabet, contractions, and accents, followed by chapters dealing with various parts of speech, including declensions of nouns and pronouns, prepositions, conjunctions, conjugation of verb tenses, and adverbs.  There are also chapters explaining the differences between "ser" and "estar" in Cebuano; comparisons; numbers; expressions of affection, money, and time; and examples of syncopes found in Cebuano.  Pages 75-78 contain a table of contents.

title: Catalogue des dessins Mexico, 1829 June-1831 October.
creator: Waldeck, Frédéric de, 1766-1875.$$QWaldeck, Frédéric de
desc: Waldeck's own descriptive catalog from June 1829, with additional notes and entries from 1830 and 1831, covering drawings he either created or acquired in Mexico between 1825 and 1831 of ancient and modern Indian subjects, their native dress, daily life, architecture, and sculptures. According to Waldeck, the drawings were made from documents at the University of Mexico, and from items held by private collectors such as Greaves and Uhde and by Waldeck himself. He describes his drawings of Mexican warriors, gods, and rulers, based on painted manuscripts or on sculpted basalt or terra cotta figures; drawings of ancient Indians from different social classes with detailed descriptions of their clothing and adornments; drawings of modern Indians--mine workers, water carriers, and tortilla makers--from such villages as Tamaulipas and Santa Catalina; landscapes; and drawings of masks, vases, sculpted symbols, and calendar wheels.  Waldeck also includes an inventory of his own collection of original Indian pictorial manuscripts (some of which are catalogued separately as Ayer Mss. 1900, 1902, 1903, 1904, and 1907).  Entries indicate the collection numbers assigned by Waldeck, with corresponding plate numbers.

title: Shawn Pfautsch papers, 2012-2014.
creator: Pfautsch, Shawn, creator.$$QPfautsch, Shawn
desc: Revised drafts of Pfautsch's play Season on the Line, also with outline cards and the music to "Jolly Is the Gale," one of the musical numbers in the play. According to Chicago Tribune critic Chris Jones, "The premise is that we were watching the unfolding of an entire season at our struggling Chicago theater company, beginning with an adaptation of 'The Great Gatsby,' moving on to Lanford Wilson's 'Balm in Gilead' and ending with a blowout, hyperexpressionistic version of 'Moby-Dick.' The backstage traumas and post-show reactions to each of these productions get their own act.....the whole piece is very much in the thrall of the Herman Melville opus." [Review, Sept. 24, 2014] The play was staged at Chicago's Chopin Theatre, September-October 2014.

title: Olga H. Huncke scrapbook of European travels, 1926 June-September.
creator: Huncke, Olga H., creator.$$QHuncke, Olga H.
desc: Scrapbook compiled by Olga H. Huncke of Chicago, Illinois, documenting her travels through Europe from June to September 1926. Huncke departed via the passenger ship R.M.S.P. Orduna in June 1926 and returned via R.M.S.P. Orca several months later in September. She traveled to many locations throughout Europe, including Paris, Versailles, Fontainebleau, and Quimper in France; Bern and Lucerne in Switzerland; Lake Como, Milan, Rome, Orvieto, Perugia, Siena, Assisi, Florence, and Venice in Italy; Vienna, Austria; Munich and Nuremberg in Germany; and Brussels, Belgium. The scrapbook consists primarily of photographs taken and ephemera collected during Huncke's travels, including postcards, programs for performances on the passenger ships and in theaters throughout Europe, travel brochures, hotel information with room numbers, clippings with images of the locations visited, menus, advertisements, business cards, visiting cards, tourist maps, receipts, and tickets. Some pages are annotated with handwritten captions and contact information, presumably of individuals whom Huncke met during her travels.

title: Revolutio alphabetaria haebrolatina [ca. 1650].
creator: Lamm, Louis, b. 1871, bookseller.$$QLamm, Louis
desc: Ms. treatise in Latin on the cabala, written in Italy, probably around 1650. Text is divided into two parts: the first, "De theorica revolutionis alphabetariae", deals with theoretical cabala, containing chapters on the word "cabala", its definition and applications, similarities for empirical cabalists in Latin and Hebrew, the use of the cabala to reveal divine prophecies, truths of the cabala, and a table of the divine names.  The second part, "De praxi revolutionis alphabetariae," focuses on practical cabala, including tables of the Hebrew alphabet, tables for converting Hebrew letters to numbers, the construction and sections of the cabalistic pyramid, the interrelationships of Triad and Tetrad, calculation of divine letters, and mystical letters.  With the text are fourteen folded leaves of tables containing alphabetical and numerical calculations in Latin and Hebrew.

creator: Edward E. Ayer Manuscript Collection (Newberry Library)$$QEdward E. Ayer Manuscript Collection (Newberry Library) | Newberry Library. Manuscript. Ayer MS 751.$$QNewberry Library.
desc: Unsigned census, possibly compiled in Acadia, and dated November 1708, of Indians and French residing on the eastern coast of Acadia, as well as those living in Pintagouet and Canibeky. The census is presented for each locale in tables of two columns.  Entries, arranged by family, and include name and age of the head of household, below which are the names and ages of wife and any children.  At the end of each section, there is a short "Recapitulation", summarizing the population numbers by sex and age, and number of households. Indian populations are given for Port Royal, Cap Sable, La Heue, Les Mines, Mouscoudabouet, Cap Breton, Chiguenitou, Pintagouet, Canibequi, and Riviere St. Jean.  Similar tables and summaries are given for French residents in Cap Sable, La Heue, and Port Rasoirs.

title: Arte de la lengua de Masinloc / que escrivió el P. Fr. Blas de Sn. Damián : año de 1755.
creator: San Damián, Blas de, 1720-ca. 1783.$$QSan Damián, Blas de
desc: Grammar in Spanish of the Sambali language spoken in the Masinloc area of Zambales province, with devotional materials in Sambali, written by Father Blas de San Damián in 1755. The first section contains explanations of the basic points of Sambali grammar, with chapters on pronunciation, the declension of nouns and pronouns, conjugations of verbs, numbers, and adverbs, interjections, and conjunctions.  Also included are a Sambali-Spanish vocabulary, an extensive list of addenda to the vocabulary, and specialized glossaries for kinship terms, months and seasons of the year, and explanations of monetary values.  The devotional materials in Sambali include a litany to the Virgen; the Viaticum; texts used in administering the sacraments of baptism, marriage, and confession; prayers such as the Paternoster, Salve Regina, and Ave Maria; and other expressions of the Catholic faith such as the Ten Commandments, the articles of faith, acts of charity, the deadly sins, and the Beatitudes.

desc: Anonymous Spanish-Zapotec phrase book, dated November 16, 1696. Phrases in Spanish, followed by their equivalents in Zapotec, are grouped together according to the situation in which they would be used, especially by a parish priest.  For example, the vocabulary lists phrases of greeting together, as well as words of consolation, accusation, expressions of anger and praise, and common questions and answers.  There are phrases for conversing with the sick, for giving instructions to Indians in the mines or fields, and for sending a servant girl to market for food.  Other sections include questions concerning the conditions and weather of a place, colors, parts of the body, numbers, kinship terms, and names of animals and places and objects in a house or a village.

title: Disertación sobre las lenguas zapoteca, chinanteca, mixe y trike y comparación con el zoke y el misteco / escrita para el Ateneo de Madrid por Francisco Belmar.
creator: Belmar, Francisco, b. 1859?$$QBelmar, Francisco
desc: Study by Francisco Belmar, dated Nov. 1, 1891 in Oaxaca de Juárez, on the grammar and vocabulary of the Zapotec, Chinantec, Mixe, and Trique languages, with comparisons to Zoque and Mixtec. Belmar's study, which he prepared for the Ateneo in Madrid in celebration of the 400th anniversary of the discovery of America, begins with an extensive list of the languages and the districts and towns in which each is spoken.  Each of the sections on the Zapotec, Chinantec, Mixe, and Trique languages includes a brief discussion of its dialects, the alphabet, basic grammar, conjugation of verb tenses, numbers, a vocabulary in some cases, and a word-by-word translation and analysis of the Lord's Prayer in the language. Belmar also includes several comparative studies: of Zapotec and Chinantec, with comparative vocabulary lists; of Mixe and Zoque; and of Trique and Mixtec.

desc: Photographic reproduction of an unsigned phrase book in Spanish and Mazateco containing common words and phrases, as well as instruction in Catholic doctrine, and texts for administering the sacraments. Common words and phrases, including those used for numbers, foods, parts of the body, clothing, building materials, and church structures and furnishing are listed in Spanish and Mazateco, arranged in double columns on each page.  Also arranged in double columns are explanations in both languages of many of the sacraments, such as confession, confirmation, communion, extreme unction, and marriage.  The section on confession contains a lengthy list of questions and answers for the priest and the penitent, based on each of the Ten Commandments.  Throughout, there are short discourses offered by the priest to explain the significance and celebration of the sacraments, as well as the necessity of living a virtuous life, maintaining humility, and obeying the clergy who are the representatives of God.

title: Apuntamto. del idioma kiché : junio 10 1854.
creator: Hernández Spina, Vicente.$$QHernández Spina, Vicente.
desc: Photographic reproduction of a copy dated June 10, 1854 of Father Vicente Hernández Spina's notes on the Quiché language, with vocabulary list. Opening sections cover the pronunciation of certain sounds unique to the Quiché language, and explain the two methods of counting in Quiché.  There is also a list of the numbers from 1 to 100 and tens and hundreds to 1000.  Hernández points out that objects unknown before the Conquest are expressed in Spanish.  The vocabulary lists are arranged randomly, with related words sometimes grouped together.  Groups include Christian names, adverbs, names of family members, pronouns, and possessives. Hernández concludes with grammar notes and examples on the declension of nouns, and plurals.

title: Arte de lengua quiche  / compuesto por N.M.R.P. Fray Bartholome. Anleo, religso. menor de N.S. Pe. San Fransco.
creator: Anleo, Bartolomé.$$QAnleo, Bartolomé.
desc: Photographic reproduction of Father Antonio Ramírez de Utrilla's 1744 copy of the Quiché grammar originally composed around 1660 by Father Bartholomé Anleo, a Franciscan priest from the Provincia del Santíssimo Nombre de Jesús de Guatemala. The first chapter on orthography focuses on the use of seven special letters to represent the sounds unique to the Quiché language.  In his subsequent discussion of the rules of Quiché grammar, Anleo states that he is following Nebrija's general outline.  He also describes the ways to express time and to count different kinds of objects, and gives the Quiché terms for numbers from 1 to 1000 and for parts of the body. The ms. concludes with a short vocabulary list of adverbial expressions.

desc: Series of unsigned, undated reading notes on various topics pertaining to the Philippines, probably written around 1853. There are references to voyages of scientific observation and hydrographic surveying, and particular mention of the discovery of the Philippines by Magellan, and the expedition of Alessandro Malaspina of 1789-1794.  Other notes discuss the Spanish conquest of the islands, and present the views of Apodaca (possibly naval commander José Ruiz de Apodaca) on the layout of the port of Manila in Manila Bay, and changes made by the English.  A list of works to consult contains such titles as "Diccionario de las Islas Filipinas;" "Quince años en las Islas Filipinas;" and Jacque Arago's Souvenirs d'un aveugle: voyage autour du monde;" as well as references to authors such as Quesada, Morata, and Antonio Saavedra.
